column2: R Red: fire and speed: direct damage, fast attacks, chaos.
G Green: nature and growth: big creatures, extra lands and lots of mana.
◇ Colorless: artifacts and some creatures fit into any deck.
The basic land for each color: Plains (white), Island (blue), Swamp (black), Mountain (red), Forest (green).
Card types
Type
What it does
Land
Produces mana. You may play one land per turn; it costs nothing.
Creature
Stays on the battlefield and can attack and block. At the bottom right are its power/toughness, e.g. 3/2: deals 3 damage, dies to 2 damage.
Sorcery
One-time effect, only during your own turn when nothing else is happening.
Instant
One-time effect, at any time, including during other players' turns as a response.
Artifact and enchantment
Stay on the battlefield and have a lasting effect, e.g. extra mana or an ongoing advantage.
Planeswalker
Powerful allies with loyalty; use one of their abilities once per turn. They can be attacked.
Reading mana and costs

The mana cost is at the top right of the card. Example: 2G means one green mana and two more of any kind. To use a land, you tap it (turn it sideways). Tapped cards are used up for this round and are turned upright again at the start of your next turn (“untapped”).
How a turn works
Untap: turn all your cards upright again.
Upkeep: effects that happen “at the beginning of your upkeep” happen now.
Draw: take one card from your library.
First main phase: play a land, cast creatures and other cards.

Combat: you choose attacking creatures (they get tapped) and whom they attack. Each player being attacked may block with untapped creatures. Unblocked damage goes to the life total; blocked creatures fight each other.
Second main phase: play cards again (e.g. whatever you didn't want to show before attacking).
End: more than seven cards in hand? Discard the extra ones. Damage on creatures wears off.
Then it's the next person's turn, clockwise.
Responding: the stack

When something is cast, everyone may respond to it, for example with an instant. Responses go “on top” and are resolved first, so the last spell cast resolves first. For a start this is enough: before a spell resolves, briefly ask whether anyone wants to respond.
Common abilities
Flying
can only be blocked by creatures with flying or reach
Haste
can attack on the turn it comes into play
Vigilance
doesn't tap to attack, so it can still block afterwards
Trample
excess damage goes through to the player despite blockers
Deathtouch
even 1 damage destroys the creature it hits
Lifelink
you gain as much life as the damage the creature deals
First strike
deals combat damage first
Hexproof
can't be the target of opponents' spells
Indestructible
isn't destroyed by damage or “destroy” effects

👑 Part 2: What makes Commander special?
A leader: your deck has a commander, usually a legendary creature. It starts in the command zone next to the battlefield and can be cast from there at any time, as if it were in your hand.

100 cards, each only once: the deck has exactly 100 cards including the commander. Each card may appear only once. Basic lands (Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest, Wastes) and cards that explicitly allow it are the exception.

Color identity: all cards must fit your commander's colors. Every mana symbol on the card counts, including in the rules text. A red-green commander therefore only allows red, green and colorless cards.
40 life instead of 20, and usually three or four people sit at the table, everyone against everyone.

Commander tax: if your commander would go to the graveyard, exile, your hand or your library, you may put it back into the command zone instead. Each further cast costs 2 more mana than the previous one.
Commander damage: a player who has taken a total of 21 combat damage from the same commander loses, no matter how much life is left.

Free mulligan: if you don't like your opening hand, shuffle and draw seven cards again. In games with several opponents the first mulligan is free; after that you put one card on the bottom of your library per mulligan.
Drawing on the first turn: in games with more than two people, the starting player also draws a card on the first turn.
Agreeing on power level

Commander is a social format: everyone should have fun. Before the game, briefly agree on how strong your decks are (“Rule 0”). There are official brackets for this (levels 1–5): from very relaxed theme decks to tournament-strength decks. Many ready-made precons are at level 2 or 3. Especially strong cards are on the Game Changer list. Manaschmiede marks them and can leave them out when building. The deck view shows your deck's level under “🎚 Bracket rating” with reasons; the detailed explanation is in the help under “Brackets”.
At a table with several players
Don't always attack the same person. Whoever is ahead becomes the target.
Deals (“I won't attack you if …”) are allowed but not binding.
Explain your cards when someone asks, and read them aloud if in doubt.
Keep life totals and commander damage visible. The 🎲 Game table does this for you.
🛠 Part 3: Your first deck
Path A: a ready-made deck (recommended for beginners)

Preconstructed Commander decks (“precons”) are playable right away and balanced against each other. Under 🎁 Precons you'll find all precons with their card lists, and under ⚔ Opponents & duel you can let them play against each other. That way you can see which one suits you before buying.
Path B: build it yourself with the assistant
Under 🛠 Build deck, click your favorite colors and/or enter a theme, e.g. “dragons”, “tokens” or “graveyard”.
“💡 Suggest commanders” shows matching commanders with images. Pick one.
“Suggest deck” puts together 100 cards. Optionally take a budget or your collection into account.
Save the deck, play a few turns alone with the sample hand and the 🎮 test board, and let it play against precons under “Opponents & duel”.

Rule of thumb for a balanced deck: about 36–38 lands, 10 cards for extra mana (“ramp”), 10 for drawing cards, 8–10 for removing single threats and 2–3 that clear the whole battlefield. The rest supports your commander's theme. Manaschmiede checks this and shows gaps.
🎲 Part 4: The first game
Setup: place the commander face up in the command zone and shuffle the other 99 cards. Open the 🎲 Game table, enter names and start the game.
Starting player: tap 🎲 in the game table and let chance decide.
Opening hand: everyone draws seven cards. Too few or too many lands (3–4 is good)? Take a mulligan.
Playing: take turns clockwise. In the first turns play lands and ramp, then cast your commander.
Counting life: in the game table tap right = +1, left = −1, hold = ±10. Enter commander damage via ⚔.
End: the last player standing wins. Choose the winner in the game table and save. This builds up your statistics.
Small glossary
Graveyard
discard pile for destroyed and used cards
Exile
cards removed from the game entirely
Library
your draw pile
Ramp
cards that give you more mana faster
Removal
cards that remove opponents' cards
Board wipe
clears all creatures (or more) from the battlefield
Token
a creature or object created by an effect, without a real card
Staple
a card found in very many decks (e.g. Sol Ring)
Combo
a few cards that together win at once or create something endless
Proxy
a placeholder printout for testing, printable from the deck and under 📦 Collection
